title:
The Girl Who
Chose Hare
description: Abandoned in the forest and rescued with a wounded hand, a girl remembers who helped her when others could not.

source.adaptation: Original Hypa retelling of the documented folktale; see SOURCES.md.

lines.text: A young woman went into the forest with her companions to gather firewood.
ask: Why does the girl go into the forest?

lines.text: She was skilled at finding good wood, and the others were jealous.
That day, she climbed a tree, slipped, and trapped her hand in the wood.
“Help me!” she cried.
But her companions left her there.
When they returned to the village, her mother asked where her daughter was.
They denied having seen her.
Alone in the forest, the young woman listened for footsteps.
Whenever she heard a sound, she sang, hoping someone would find her.
A hunter heard her voice.
Frightened by singing in the lonely forest, he fled.
But he remembered the song and eventually brought it back to the village.
Her family recognised it.
ask: How does her family find her?

lines.text: They gathered people, machetes, and tools, and followed the hunter into the forest.
When the young woman sang again, voices answered.
They cut away the wood and freed her.
But her hand was badly wounded.
At home, her mother watched her suffering and feared she would never recover.
In desperation, she promised that whoever healed her daughter could marry her.
The animals came to try.
Monkey tried, but failed.
Panther could not heal her.
Lion could not help either.
Then Hare stepped forward.
Those around him doubted him.
Others had already failed.
What could Hare possibly do?
At last, her mother allowed him to try.
Using remedies from the surrounding land, Hare treated the wound.
His efforts succeeded, and the young woman recovered.
Soon suitors began to arrive.
Some were wealthy.
Others belonged to important families.
Each hoped she would choose him.
She refused them.
Instead, she chose Hare.
People were surprised.
Why refuse wealth and rank for him?
But the young woman remembered who had helped her when she was suffering.
An important name had not healed her.
Riches had not healed her.
Hare had succeeded when others could not.
She chose him and honoured her mother’s promise.
Her companions had let jealousy turn them against her.
Others had doubted Hare before seeing what he could do.
But she remembered his help.
And so she married Hare, choosing the one whose deeds mattered most to her.
